subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Default Effect in Marketing
description: Learn Default Effect in Marketing in one minute.

hook.text: A software company pre-checked the annual plan. 70% of users kept it. When monthly was default, only 30% chose annual.

buildup.text: Defaults are the choice you get if you do nothing. Most people accept them because changing requires effort.

discovery.text: Johnson and Goldstein showed organ donation rates differ by 60 percentage points based purely on whether opt-in.

twist.text: Pre-checked boxes for newsletters, add-ons, and insurance exploit this. You agree by not disagreeing.

climax.text: Before submitting any form, uncheck every pre-checked box and re-check only what you genuinely want.

punchline.text: The default is someone else's preference, not yours.

quiz.question: Why are defaults so powerful in marketing?
options: Defaults are always the best option
Most people accept them because changing requires effort
Laws require companies to set optimal defaults

details.summary: The default effect in marketing leverages people's strong tendency to stick with pre-selected options. By setting the desired option as the default, marketers dramatically increase its adoption because switching requires effort that most consumers avoid.
details.whyItMatters: Defaults are one of the most powerful tools in behavioral marketing because they exploit status quo bias and effort aversion. From subscription tiers to privacy settings, whoever sets the default often determines the outcome.
takeaways: People overwhelmingly stick with pre-selected default options
Defaults exploit status quo bias and effort aversion simultaneously
Ethical defaults align company interests with customer well-being

faq.question: How powerful is the default effect in practice?
faq.answer: Extremely powerful. Organ donation rates jump from 15 to 90 percent when switched from opt-in to opt-out. Software add-on acceptance rises from 10 to 70 percent when pre-checked. Defaults routinely shift behavior by 50 or more percentage points.

faq.question: When is using defaults in marketing ethical?
faq.answer: Defaults are ethical when they genuinely benefit the customer and are easy to change. They become manipulative when they exploit inertia to trap customers in unwanted subscriptions, services, or terms they would not actively choose.
